report: The patient has progressive dyspnea, hypoxia, elevated JVP, pulmonary crackles, and edema. Chest X-ray shows severe bilateral pulmonary congestion, and echocardiography reveals LVEF 35%, confirming heart failure with reduced ejection fraction as the cause of cardiogenic volume overload. Pulmonary embolism and gastroenteritis/dehydration are excluded by absent chest pain/syncope and clear hypervolemia. Diarrhea is explained by congestive gastroenteropathy from bowel congestion. Acute renal failure with severe hyperkalemia (K 9.0, Cr 2.8) complicates the picture in this renal transplant patient. The graph shows HFrEF supporting cardiogenic volume overload, with acute renal failure and congestive gastroenteropathy as complications; the frontier is sufficiently refined.
